sections.title: Create a square-lattice part
sections.body: Sweep carries a lattice cross-section along a spline. This example uses the same three rows × six columns (18 helices) as the Extrude guide, with a path defined in nanometers.

sections.title: Choose the source and plane
sections.body: Open Tools → Sweep. From selects a new bundle or an existing helix end. For this example choose New bundle and XY. Plane sets the initial cross-section; choose it before selecting cells, because changing planes clears the footprint.

sections.title: Select the 3×6 cross-section
sections.body: The picker faces the selected plane and shares the Extrude selection gestures. Select rows 0–2 and columns 1–6: 18 helices. Drag the tool window by its title bar if it covers your intended cells.

sections.title: Choose strands and ligation
sections.body: Include chooses Both, Scaffold or Staples. Ligate adjacent requests joining compatible strand ends when continuing a source. Use Both with Ligate adjacent checked for this example.

sections.title: Define the path in nanometers
sections.body: Click Next to leave the cross-section picker and define the path in 3D. XYZ values are offsets in nm from the cross-section center. Select a point in the list to edit it. The initial XY path runs from Origin (0, 0, 0) to Point 1 (0, 0, 10). Previous returns to cross-section selection while retaining the path.

sections.title: Control direction and twist
sections.body: Select a point, then enable Control direction and twist to set Tilt X, Tilt Y and Twist in degrees. Green arrows indicate direction and amber arrows indicate the right axis. Disabling the checkbox restores automatic orientation. Selected points also have position handles in the canvas; Tab on the canvas or point entry switches to free-angle rotation handles.

sections.title: Review and confirm
sections.body: The status reports path length in nm and bp per helix. New BP reports the total new base-pair sites across the selected cross-section. Review any curvature warning before confirming; adjust the path if needed. Confirm creates the swept bundle.

steps.caption: Choose File → New.
Choose Square for the lattice type. The guide uses a temporary example name; use a meaningful name for your own part.
Click Create to open the empty square-lattice part.
Use Full representation throughout this guide. Full shows the nucleotide beads and base slabs; it is the standard display for guides.
Open Tools → Sweep.
Keep From set to New bundle.
Choose XY for a cross-section initially normal to Z. XZ and YZ are also available.
Click a cell to select it. Click the same cell again to deselect it.

With the canvas focused, press Tab for box selection. Left-drag from upper left to lower right, enclosing the entire circles of the 3-row × 6-column footprint. Left-to-right requires full enclosure; right-to-left selects touching cells.
The count must read 18 helices. Tab returns to ordinary cell picking; a left-drag can also paint cells along its path.
Choose Scaffold to create only scaffold strands.
Choose Staples to create only staple strands.
Choose Both for this example.
Keep Ligate adjacent checked. The new-bundle example has no upstream ends to join.
Click Next to open Step 2: Define sweep path.
With Point 1 selected, set Z to 30 nm. Keep X = 0 and Y = 0.
Click + Add point. The new point extrapolates the last segment and becomes selected.
For Point 2 enter X = 12, Y = 0, Z = 60 nm. The spline bends toward positive X. Scroll down over the canvas to zoom out as the path grows.
Review the ordered path: Origin (0, 0, 0), Point 1 (0, 0, 30), Point 2 (12, 0, 60). The × beside a non-origin point deletes it; a path needs at least two points.
Enable Control direction and twist for Point 2.
Enter 15° in Twist to inspect the end cross-section orientation.
Disable Control direction and twist to use automatic orientation for the final example.
Read New BP and the path-length status for the 18 selected helices.
Click Confirm to build the sweep.
The completed 3×6 bundle follows the curved path. Right-drag to orbit and press F to fit the result; Full representation shows the nucleotide geometry.
